correctness.rationale: Complete finite enumeration across all 27 singleton, 351 pair and 2925 triple seeds establishes the optimum 3 and 567 states. Exact legal move construction and BFS across all 160461 unordered state pairs prove all graph metrics and distance differences. Separate Python and C++ implementations reconstruct isomorphic graphs using coordinate and Cayley constructions and agree on the full enumeration; a third program checks all 54 automorphisms and the orbit partition. No infinite quantifier is asserted.

evidence: The inspected 2022 paper gives general power-domination TAR/TJ theory and specific families including complete graphs, bicliques, cycles, paths and wheels.
Its relevant PDF sections contain no Doyle/Holt graph treatment; the paper does not state a general formula from which 567 optima or the sharp slide penalty follows.
The 2018 polynomial paper is a general counting source; only its abstract was inspected, so it cannot be excluded as a full-text source of data.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broad theorems about connectedness or universal realization do not determine exact optimum counts, full slide-graph metrics or paired-distance multiplicities for this graph. The more general polynomial article was not used for a negative full-text comparison.

value.rationale: The Doyle–Holt graph is the unique smallest half-arc-transitive graph, giving a motivated finite testbed for optimization under asymmetric local geometry. Its complete optimum-census, 11-orbit structure, two latency classes and especially 54 one-jump pairs needing six local slides are nontrivial exact reconfiguration invariants with natural benchmarking value; no unrelated arbitrary slice or unsupported universal significance is claimed.
